# nish/crypto/jwt

JSON Web Tokens in the JWS compact serialization: verify one and check its claims, or sign one. RFC 7519 (JWT), RFC 7515 (JWS), RFC 7518 (the HS, RS and ES algorithms), RFC 8037 (EdDSA) and the RFC 8725 best current practice.

```ts
import {
  JWT_ALG_EDDSA,
  JWT_ALG_ES256,
  JWT_ALG_ES384,
  JWT_ALG_HS256,
  JWT_ALG_HS384,
  JWT_ALG_HS512,
  JWT_ALG_RS256,
  JWT_ALG_RS384,
  JWT_ALG_RS512,
  JWT_ERR_ALG,
  JWT_ERR_AUDIENCE,
  JWT_ERR_CLAIMS,
  JWT_ERR_EXPIRED,
  JWT_ERR_FORMAT,
  JWT_ERR_HEADER,
  JWT_ERR_IAT,
  JWT_ERR_ISSUER,
  JWT_ERR_NOT_YET,
  JWT_ERR_SIGNATURE,
  JWT_ERR_SIZE,
  JWT_ERR_SUBJECT,
  JWT_ERR_TYPE,
  JWT_MAX_TOKEN,
  JWT_MAX_TOKEN_LIMIT,
  JWT_OK,
  JwtKey,
  JwtVerifier,
  jwtAlgName,
  jwtEcKey,
  jwtEd25519Key,
  jwtEd25519SigningKey,
  jwtEs256SigningKey,
  jwtHmacKey,
  jwtRsaKey,
  jwtRsaKeyParts,
  jwtSign,
  jwtSignKid,
  jwtSignString,
} from "nish/crypto/jwt";
```

<scalar-code-group>

```ts example.ts
import { Secret } from "nish:secret";
import { JWT_ALG_HS256, JWT_MAX_TOKEN, JWT_OK, JwtKey, JwtVerifier, jwtHmacKey, jwtSignString } from "nish/crypto/jwt";

// secretKey: at least 32 random bytes, still the caller's to wipe; now: seconds since 1970
const roundTrip = (secretKey: Secret<u8[]>, token: string, now: i64): string | null => {
  const key: JwtKey | null = jwtHmacKey(JWT_ALG_HS256, secretKey); // make once; null for a short key
  if (key === null) {
    return null;
  }
  const v = new JwtVerifier(JWT_MAX_TOKEN); // make once per thread
  v.issuer = "https://issuer.example";
  v.audience = "api";
  v.leeway = toI64(30);
  if (v.verifyString(key, token, now) === JWT_OK) {
    // v.claims[0 .. v.claimsLen) is the payload's JSON; v.exp, v.nbf, v.iat are read
  }
  const minted: string | null = jwtSignString(key, "{\"sub\":\"ana\"}");
  key.wipe();
  return minted;
};
```

</scalar-code-group>

<scalar-detail title="The key decides the algorithm, never the token">

A `JwtKey` is made for
one algorithm, and a token verifies only when its header's `alg` is that
algorithm's name, spelled exactly. `none` names no key, so a token that says
it is unsigned is refused like any other mismatch (`JWT_ERR_ALG`); an `HS256`
header in front of an RSA key is refused before any MAC is taken, so an RSA
public key can never be used as an HMAC secret (RFC 8725 §2.1, §3.1).

The header must hold `alg` exactly once, as a string; `typ` and `kid` at most
once, as strings; and no `crit` and no `b64` (RFC 7515 §4.1.11, RFC 7797),
since this verifier understands no extension and a header that names one must
be refused. Other header members are skipped.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Nothing in the payload is read before the signature holds">

The verifier
reads the header, decodes the signature and checks it, and only then decodes
and parses the claims. The claims are then checked against the clock and the
verifier's settings:

- `exp` (RFC 7519 §4.1.4): the token is good while `now - leeway < exp`.
  A token with no `exp` is refused unless `requireExp` is cleared.
- `nbf` (§4.1.5): good once `nbf <= now + leeway`.
- `iat` (§4.1.6): refused when it is later than `now + leeway`.
- `iss`, `sub` (§4.1.1, §4.1.2): when the verifier names one, the token must
  carry it, spelled exactly.
- `aud` (§4.1.3): one string or an array of strings. When the verifier names
  an audience, one of them must be it. A token that carries `aud` is refused
  by a verifier that names none, as §4.1.3 requires.

</scalar-detail>

Each registered claim may appear once; the time claims are integers
(seconds since 1970). `now` is the caller's, so a test passes its own clock.

<scalar-detail title="Bounded once made">

A `JwtVerifier` holds its decode buffers, its
tokenizer and its results, sized once from the largest token it takes
(`JWT_MAX_TOKEN` by default, 8 KiB); a longer token is refused before a
byte is decoded. An HS token is checked against `HmacKey`'s pads, keyed
once when the key was made, through `hmacKeyedVerify`, and the tag is
compared in constant time: an HS verify allocates nothing past its arena
block. An RS, ES or EdDSA verify allocates the signed input's copy and
whatever the public-key check itself allocates (bignums, points), which
the caller's scope releases. One verifier is one thread's: it is not safe
to share while a `verify` runs.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Base64url is strict">

**Base64url is strict**, as `nish/crypto/base64url`: no padding, no
whitespace, no character outside `A-Z a-z 0-9 - _`, and no stray bits in the
last character, so each token has one spelling. The token itself is public,
so the decoder here branches freely.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Signing">

**Signing** covers HS256/384/512, ES256 and EdDSA, the algorithms the
standard library holds a signer for; `jwtSign` answers `null` for an RS or
ES384 key, which can verify only. The header written is
`{"alg":"…","typ":"JWT"}`, with a `kid` when one is given.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Secrets">

An HMAC key and a private key are `Secret<u8[]>`
(`nish:secret`). A `JwtKey` copies what it is handed and the caller still
owns, and wipes, its own; `JwtKey.wipe()` zeroes the key's copy and its HMAC
pads. The threat model and what was checked are in
`docs/security/crypto-jwt.md`.

</scalar-detail>

Private names carry the `jwt` prefix because a `std/` module's private
functions share the importing program's flat symbol namespace
(`docs/wp26-stdlib.md` §3e).

## Functions

### jwtAlgName

The `alg` header value for `alg`, `""` for no algorithm this module knows.

```ts
function jwtAlgName(alg: i32): string
```

<scalar-field name="alg" type="i32" required>

A `JWT_ALG_` constant.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string">

The name RFC 7518 or RFC 8037 spells it with, such as `"HS256"`.

</scalar-field>

### jwtEcKey

An ES256 or ES384 verifying key from its uncompressed point, `04 ‖ x ‖ y`
(65 or 97 bytes). A point of the wrong length or form answers `null`; one
off the curve makes every verification fail.

```ts
function jwtEcKey(
  alg: i32,
  point: u8[],
): JwtKey | null
```

<scalar-field name="alg" type="i32" required>

`JWT_ALG_ES256` or `JWT_ALG_ES384`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="point" type="u8[]" required>

The public point, copied into the key.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="JwtKey | null">

A new key that verifies only, or `null`.

</scalar-field>

### jwtEd25519Key

An EdDSA (Ed25519) verifying key from its 32 bytes (RFC 8037 §2's `x`);
another length answers `null`.

```ts
function jwtEd25519Key(pub: u8[]): JwtKey | null
```

<scalar-field name="pub" type="u8[]" required>

The public key, copied into the key.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="JwtKey | null">

A new key that verifies only, or `null`.

</scalar-field>

### jwtEd25519SigningKey

An EdDSA key that signs and verifies, from its 32-byte seed (RFC 8037 §2's
`d`). A seed of another length answers `null`. The key keeps a copy; `seed`
stays the caller's to wipe.

```ts
function jwtEd25519SigningKey(
  seed: Secret<u8[]>,
): JwtKey | null
```

<scalar-field name="seed" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;" required>

The private seed.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="JwtKey | null">

A new key that signs and verifies, or `null`.

</scalar-field>

### jwtEs256SigningKey

An ES256 key that signs and verifies, from its 32-byte private scalar. A
scalar `p256PublicKey` refuses answers `null`. The key keeps a copy;
`priv` stays the caller's to wipe.

```ts
function jwtEs256SigningKey(
  priv: Secret<u8[]>,
): JwtKey | null
```

<scalar-field name="priv" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;" required>

The private scalar, big-endian.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="JwtKey | null">

A new key that signs and verifies, or `null`.

</scalar-field>

### jwtHmacKey

An HS256, HS384 or HS512 key that verifies and signs. RFC 7518 §3.2 asks for
a key at least as long as the hash, so a shorter one answers `null`, as does
an `alg` that is not HS. The pads are keyed once, here; `key` stays the
caller's to wipe.

```ts
function jwtHmacKey(
  alg: i32,
  key: Secret<u8[]>,
): JwtKey | null
```

<scalar-field name="alg" type="i32" required>

`JWT_ALG_HS256`, `JWT_ALG_HS384` or `JWT_ALG_HS512`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="key" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;" required>

The shared secret: at least 32, 48 or 64 bytes for the three.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="JwtKey | null">

A new key that verifies and signs, or `null`.

</scalar-field>

### jwtRsaKey

An RS256, RS384 or RS512 key from the DER of a PKCS#1 `RSAPublicKey`
(`rsaParsePublicKey`'s input). A key that does not parse, a modulus below
2048 bits (RFC 7518 §3.3) or an `alg` that is not RS answers `null`.

```ts
function jwtRsaKey(
  alg: i32,
  der: u8[],
): JwtKey | null
```

<scalar-field name="alg" type="i32" required>

`JWT_ALG_RS256`, `JWT_ALG_RS384` or `JWT_ALG_RS512`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="der" type="u8[]" required>

The public key's DER, nothing before it and nothing after it.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="JwtKey | null">

A new key that verifies only, or `null`.

</scalar-field>

### jwtRsaKeyParts

An RS key from its big-endian modulus and exponent, as a JWK's `n` and `e`
spell them once base64url-decoded (RFC 7518 §6.3.1). The same checks as
`jwtRsaKey`; parts too long for any key this module takes answer `null`.

```ts
function jwtRsaKeyParts(
  alg: i32,
  n: u8[],
  e: u8[],
): JwtKey | null
```

<scalar-field name="alg" type="i32" required>

`JWT_ALG_RS256`, `JWT_ALG_RS384` or `JWT_ALG_RS512`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="n" type="u8[]" required>

The modulus, big-endian; leading zero bytes are dropped.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="e" type="u8[]" required>

The public exponent, big-endian; leading zero bytes are dropped.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="JwtKey | null">

A new key that verifies only, or `null`.

</scalar-field>

### jwtSign

`jwtSignKid` with no `kid`.

```ts
function jwtSign(
  key: JwtKey,
  claims: u8[],
): string | null
```

<scalar-field name="key" type="JwtKey" required>

The key to sign with.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="claims" type="u8[]" required>

The payload: one JSON object, in bytes.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string | null">

The token, or `null` as `jwtSignKid` answers it.

</scalar-field>

### jwtSignKid

A compact JWS over the JSON object `claims`, signed with `key`, with a
`kid` header member when `kid` is not `null`. Answers `null` when `key`
cannot sign (RS, ES384 or a verify-only key), when `claims` is not one JSON
object, or when `kid` is empty, longer than 256 bytes, or holds a byte that
would need a JSON escape. The claims are signed as given: this function
neither adds nor checks any claim.

```ts
function jwtSignKid(
  key: JwtKey,
  kid: string | null,
  claims: u8[],
): string | null
```

<scalar-field name="key" type="JwtKey" required>

The key to sign with; a wiped one answers `null`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="kid" type="string | null" required>

The key id to name in the header, or `null` for none.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="claims" type="u8[]" required>

The payload: one JSON object, in bytes.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string | null">

The token, a new string, or `null`.

</scalar-field>

### jwtSignString

`jwtSign` over the bytes of the string `claims`. Answers `null` for claims
outside ASCII, as `verifyString` refuses them: escape such text (`\u00e9`)
or pass its UTF-8 bytes to `jwtSign`.

```ts
function jwtSignString(
  key: JwtKey,
  claims: string,
): string | null
```

<scalar-field name="key" type="JwtKey" required>

The key to sign with.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="claims" type="string" required>

The payload: one JSON object, ASCII.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string | null">

The token, or `null` as `jwtSignKid` answers it.

</scalar-field>

## Classes

### JwtKey

A key for one algorithm: what verifies its tokens and, for a key that can,
signs them. Make one with `jwtHmacKey`, `jwtRsaKey`, `jwtRsaKeyParts`,
`jwtEcKey`, `jwtEd25519Key`, `jwtEs256SigningKey` or
`jwtEd25519SigningKey`; `wipe()` it when it is done with. An HS key holds
its HMAC work hashers, so a key is one thread's, like a `JwtVerifier`: give
each worker its own.

```ts
class JwtKey
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new JwtKey(alg: i32, hmac: HmacKey \| null, rsa: RsaPublicKey \| null, pub: u8[], priv: Secret<u8[]>, canSign: boolean)` | A key from its parts, checked for nothing: the `jwt…Key` functions are the way to make one, and this exists for them and for tests that build a key no function would. `hmac`, `rsa` and `pub` are kept as given; `priv` is copied, and stays the caller's to wipe. |
| `wipe(): void` | Zero the key's private copy and its HMAC pads. It neither signs nor verifies after: its zeroed secret is one anyone could hold. |

### JwtVerifier

Verifies compact JWS tokens and checks their claims, reusing its buffers:
make one per thread and call `verify` per token. The settings are public
fields, read on every `verify`. After `JWT_OK`, `claims[0 .. claimsLen)`
is the payload's JSON for the caller's own claims, and `exp`, `nbf` and
`iat` hold the time claims when `hasExp`, `hasNbf` and `hasIat` say so.
`claims` and `sig` are the verifier's own buffers, not copies: the next
`verify` overwrites them.

```ts
class JwtVerifier
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new JwtVerifier(maxToken: i32)` | A verifier for tokens of up to `maxToken` bytes; outside `[16, JWT_MAX_TOKEN_LIMIT]` panics. Every buffer is allocated here, once. |
| `audience: string \| null` | The audience a token's `aud` must name, or `null` to refuse a token with any `aud`. |
| `readonly claims: u8[]` | The decoded payload of the last token, `claimsLen` bytes of it valid after `JWT_OK`. |
| `claimsLen: i32` | How many bytes of `claims` are the payload: its length after `JWT_OK`, 0 after any refusal. |
| `exp: i64` | The last token's `exp`, in seconds since 1970; meaningful only when `hasExp`. |
| `hasExp: boolean` | Whether the last token's payload carried `exp`. Cleared at the start of each `verify` and set as the claims are read, so a token refused for its claims may leave it set. |
| `hasIat: boolean` | Whether the last token's payload carried `iat`, as `hasExp`. |
| `hasNbf: boolean` | Whether the last token's payload carried `nbf`, as `hasExp`. |
| `iat: i64` | The last token's `iat`, in seconds since 1970; meaningful only when `hasIat`. |
| `issuer: string \| null` | The `iss` a token must carry, or `null` for any. |
| `leeway: i64` | Seconds of clock skew allowed to `exp`, `nbf` and `iat`; held to `[0, 2^31 - 1]`. |
| `readonly maxToken: i32` | The largest token taken, in bytes. |
| `nbf: i64` | The last token's `nbf`, in seconds since 1970; meaningful only when `hasNbf`. |
| `requireExp: boolean` | Whether a token without `exp` is refused; on by default. |
| `readonly sig: u8[]` | The last token's signature, decoded, at the front; `JWT_MAX_SIGNATURE` bytes long, whatever the signature's own length. It is written only once the header passes, so after a refusal before that it still holds an earlier token's bytes. |
| `subject: string \| null` | The `sub` a token must carry, or `null` for any. |
| `typ: string \| null` | The header `typ` a token must carry (RFC 8725 §3.11), or `null` for any. |
| `peekKid(src: u8[], off: i32, len: i32, out: u8[]): i32` | The header's `kid` of the token `src[off .. off + len)`, written at `out[0 ..)`: its length, or -1 when the token is malformed, has no `kid` or its `kid` does not fit `out`. This reads the header **before** any signature is checked, so it only chooses which key to verify with; the `kid` proves nothing until `verify` answers `JWT_OK` under that key. |
| `verify(key: JwtKey, src: u8[], off: i32, len: i32, now: i64): i32` | Verifies the token `src[off .. off + len)` under `key` and checks its claims at `now` (seconds since 1970): `JWT_OK`, or the first `JWT_ERR_*` that applies, in this order:<br>- the window (`JWT_ERR_SIZE`);<br>- the three parts and the header's base64url (`JWT_ERR_FORMAT`);<br>- the header's members in the order written (`JWT_ERR_HEADER`, `JWT_ERR_ALG`), then a missing `alg` and, when the verifier names a `typ`, a missing or other one;<br>- signature text too long for any signature (`JWT_ERR_SIGNATURE`);<br>- the signature's base64url (`JWT_ERR_FORMAT`);<br>- its length, the key's fit and the signature itself (`JWT_ERR_SIGNATURE`);<br>- the payload's base64url (`JWT_ERR_FORMAT`);<br>- the payload's members in the order written and, while `requireExp` is set (the default), a missing `exp` (`JWT_ERR_CLAIMS`);<br>- and then `exp`, `nbf`, `iat`, `iss`, `aud` and `sub`, in that order. |
| `verifyString(key: JwtKey, token: string, now: i64): i32` | `verify` on the bytes of `token`, copied into the verifier's own buffer first; a token longer than `maxToken` is refused before the copy. |

<scalar-card title="-10" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">
